limits: Synthetic provider contracts plus real own coded scene; not an original-device corpus or native Gallery acceptance.
Raw metadata extraction emits explicit complete source blocks; proprietary blocks can include coded media.
Declarations are not validated motion assets; Rust reports these independently.
Pinned Google does not classify namespace-equivalent c:/o: aliases in these legacy/OpCamera attribute cases; canonical GCamera:/OpCamera: cases are checked independently.
Pinned HeifContainerSplitter::Split emits XMP only when mpvd exists; Rust also exposes ordinary-image metadata and explicitly distinguishes declarations from verified motion.

For malformed Honor OfflineData with a missing length prefix, Google skips four bytes and scans for sceneMode; Rust reports malformed-trailer diagnostics and retains the full raw source block. A separate correctly length-prefixed metadata-only case verifies sceneMode and tag semantics.

differences: Google does not assign component-mix values; Rust preserves their encoded coefficients without inventing weights.
Google returns partial/default results for truncated curves; Rust rejects truncation.
Google JSON projects one rule; Rust retains every rule and exposes that limited projection separately.
Rust retains absent fields as None and unknown descriptors/raw flag bits; it does not create default score/timestamp objects.
Semantic validation is explicit, including score range, ordering and exact photo-time consistency.
No Moments construction API is implemented.

timed.scope: Google Mp4BoxReader primitive actually used by MetadataEngine, not all facade/device behavior
differences: Pinned Google selects by stts, omits ctts/edit mapping and clamps after the last sample.
Rust honors composition and exact unit-rate edits, returns no sample outside half-open intervals, and preserves raw packet bytes.
